greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the quiet presence of the Lord, seeking to hear His voice in the stillness of our own hearts.
penitential:
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
homily:
There is a quiet, steady rhythm to the way the heart learns to trust. It is not a loud, sudden realization that changes everything in a flash of light. Rather, it is like watching a stream find its way over rocks. The first reading today from Proverbs gives us this image: 'Like a stream is the king’s heart in the hand of the LORD; wherever it pleases him, he directs it.'

Think of the way a stream moves. It does not fight the terrain; it yields to it. It follows the path laid out by the earth, carving its way through the landscape, always moving, always flowing toward the sea. We often want our lives to be like a paved road—straight, predictable, and within our control. We want to know exactly where the path leads and how long the journey will take. But the life of faith is more like that stream. It is a movement of the heart, directed by the hand of God, often through places we would not have chosen for ourselves.

Benjamin Vo knew something about paths and journeys. He was a boy who looked at the world as a vast, interconnected map. Whether he was exploring the streets of Tokyo, the grottoes of Lourdes, or simply sitting with his father, mapping out the logistics of a future flight, he had a mind that loved to see how things were connected. He had a natural, intuitive curiosity that made him want to understand the 'why' and the 'how' of the world around him. He was a boy who loved to dream, and that dream of 'con chim airlines'—that little, hopeful name for a company that would one day take flight—was a testament to a spirit that was always looking toward the horizon.

But today, the Gospel of Luke brings us to a different kind of boundary. The mother of Jesus and his brothers are standing outside, unable to reach him because of the crowd. They want to see him. They want to connect. And Jesus, in a moment that seems startling at first, says: 'My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and act on it.'

He is not pushing his family away. He is expanding the definition of family. He is saying that the deepest, most enduring bond is not found in blood or in proximity, but in the shared life of the Word. To hear the Word and to act on it—that is the stream that leads us home. That is the path that connects us, even when we are separated by the greatest distances.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, your hearts have been tracing the path of a stream that has led you into a valley of profound, quiet sorrow. You look at the photos—perhaps that one of Ben standing in his Lakers jersey in front of the temple tower, flashing that peaceful, two-finger sign, with a smile that seemed to hold the secret of a quiet joy—and you feel the ache of the distance. You wonder where the stream is leading. You wonder how to keep walking when the path seems to have disappeared into the mist. But hear the promise of the Gospel today. You are not standing outside. You are already part of the family of God. You are already in the circle of those who hear the Word and act on it. Your love for Benjamin, and the way you continue to honor his life—that is your way of acting on the Word. That is your way of keeping the stream moving.

Ryan, my dear brother, you know this better than anyone. You are the one who shared the adventures, the laughter, and the quiet moments of growing up. When you feel the weight of his absence, remember that the bond between you is not a memory. It is a living, breathing reality in the heart of God. You carry his spirit in your own, and every time you choose to be curious, every time you choose to be kind, every time you look at the world with the same wonder that he did, you are carrying his legacy forward. You are the brother who knows that love is the only thing that truly lasts. Keep dreaming, Ryan. Keep being the boy who knows that the world is a big, beautiful place, and that you are never walking through it alone.

I want to speak to those of you who might be carrying a hidden, heavy stone of self-reproach. Maybe you find yourself replaying the past, wondering if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. Please, hear this truth today: God does not send these seasons of sorrow as a punishment, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he loved. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the past, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

There is a profound, healing truth in the Psalm we prayed today: 'The way of truth I have chosen; I have set your ordinances before me.' Benjamin chose the way of kindness. He chose the way of curiosity. He chose the way of love. And that choice is not lost. It is woven into the very fabric of the Kingdom. When you see the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, when you see the way his kindness continues to flow into the lives of those who have never met him, you are seeing the truth of the Gospel. His life is still bearing fruit. It is still feeding the hungry. It is still quenching the thirst of those who have nothing. His love is not a memory; it is an action. It is a sign that the Kingdom is already here, and that the love we share is never lost.

Do you remember how he was always the first to greet his father? How he would never forget a 'Good morning, Dad'? That was not just a habit; it was a way of honoring the people he loved. It was a way of saying, 'I am here, and I am present to you.' That is what Jesus is asking of us today. He is asking us to be present to Him, to be present to one another, and to be present to the love that he has planted in our hearts. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but a real thing. When the world feels too quiet, when the grief feels like it is choking the joy out of the day, do not try to fix it. Do not try to solve the mystery. Just be like the stream. Let yourself be directed by the hand of the Lord. When you feel the ache, whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your prayer. You are a family of four, and you are being led, step by step, through the darkness and into the light. The reunion is certain. And in the meantime, keep walking in the presence of God, in the light of the living. He is there, he is waiting, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are not walking alone. You are walking toward the Banquet, where all the laborers are gathered, where all the tears are wiped away, and where the love you shared will bloom forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His light shine upon you always. Go in peace.
standing_petitions: For our dear Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ.
For all families who carry the weight of grief, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of eternal reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Like a stream is the king’s heart in the hand of the LORD;
wherever it pleases him, he directs it.All the ways of a man may be right in his own eyes,
but it is the LORD who proves hearts.To do what is right and just
is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.Haughty eyes and a proud heart–
the tillage of the wicked is sin.The plans of the diligent are sure of profit,
but all rash haste leads certainly to poverty.Whoever makes a fortune by a lying tongue
is chasing a bubble over deadly snares.The soul of the wicked man desires evil;
his neighbor finds no pity in his eyes.When the arrogant man is punished, the simple are the wiser;
when the wise man is instructed, he gains knowledge.The just man appraises the house of the wicked:
there is one who brings down the wicked to ruin.He who shuts his ear to the cry of the poor
will himself also call and not be heard.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (35) Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
Blessed are they whose way is blameless,
who walk in the law of the LORD.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
Make me understand the way of your precepts,
and I will meditate on your wondrous deeds.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
The way of truth I have chosen;
I have set your ordinances before me.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
Give me discernment, that I may observe your law
and keep it with all my heart.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
Lead me in the path of your commands,
for in it I delight.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.
And I will keep your law continually,
forever and ever.
R. Guide me, Lord, in the way of your commands.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
The mother of Jesus and his brothers came to him
but were unable to join him because of the crowd.
He was told, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside
and they wish to see you.”
He said to them in reply, “My mother and my brothers 
are those who hear the word of God and act on it.”

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm
